chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Urama, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Minqari, from Yunus ibn Abi Yaqzan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Walk in front of the coffin of the knowledgeable Muslim, and do not walk in front of the coffin of the denier (of faith), for indeed, in front of the coffin of the Muslim are angels hastening him to Paradise, and indeed, in front of the coffin of the disbeliever are angels hastening him to the Fire.

key_terms.الْعَارِف: The knowledgeable (one with deep religious insight)

ai.seo_question: Why should one walk in front of a knowledgeable Muslim's coffin but not a disbeliever's?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi distinguishes between the 'Muslim' (one with deep gnosis or 'Arif') and the 'denier' (Kafir), linking the physical act of walking order to the metaphysical reality of angels escorting the soul. In Shia tradition, this underscores that spiritual rank, not just ritual affiliation, determines the honor accorded in death, reflecting the belief that the deceased's inner state influences their immediate post-mortem journey.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Owrama, from Muhammad Bin Amro, from Husayn Bin Ahmad Al Minqary, from Yunus Bin Zibyan,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Walk in front of a coffin of the learned Muslim but do not walk in front of a coffin of the rejecter (of Eman), for in front of a coffin of the Muslim would be Angels hastening with him to the Paradise, and in front of the coffin of the unbeliever would be Angels hastening with him to the Fire’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn ‘Uramah from Muhammad ibn ‘Amr from Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Minqariy from Yunus ibn Zabyan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Walk in front of the coffin of a knowledgeable Muslim but do not walk in front of the coffin of a rejecter (of belief). In front of the coffin of a Muslim, angels who hasten to paradise walk, but in front of the coffin of an unbeliever, angels walk who hasten with him (the unbeliever) to hell.”’
